entries.scientificReason: Dark germination is a valid counterexample to a universal all-seeds light necessity claim. Controlled15-to25°C enzyme differences support a bounded hypothesis; a70°C fall does not refute that particular interval.
entries.heterogeneityReason: universal biological claim versus conditional interval-specific claim
entries.visualReason: Fresh pale dark-germinated seedlings can counter a claim that germination requires light; they are not indefinitely healthy dark-grown plants. The opened box is a viewing moment, not a light-tight working setup. Caption should identify the necessity claim so pale leaves are not misread as counterevidence to light-dependent greening.
entries.readabilityPerspectiveAndFormat: Hypothese and Gegenbefund readable at360; pale seedlings and green light-grown seedlings are visually distinct.
entries.actualJudgmentOrigin: unchanged genuine original native14 first judgment

Cube area/volume6 and3 inverse-length ratios are correct, and folded area60/volume8=7.5 does not guarantee a respiratory performance.

entries.scientificReason: Observer classification includes operational criteria, independent coding, reanalysis versus biological replication, falsifiability, consistency and provisionality. Conditional herbivore advantage is contrasted with an untestable nature-wants explanation; absent pressure does not refute the conditional claim.
entries.heterogeneityReason: microscopic observation reliability versus evolutionary field inference
entries.visualReason: Two groups with prepared stage samples compare leaf/model observations and ask new questions. Schematic paired curves are not actual repeat data or proof of reproducibility; foreground leaves are preparation context rather than a microscopic image.
entries.readabilityPerspectiveAndFormat: Wiederholen, Vergleichen and Weiterfragen readable at360; scopes align with eyes, tablet backs face viewer while screens face learners; iterative arrows are clear.
entries.actualJudgmentOrigin: unchanged genuine original native14 first judgment
